answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond in the plume ledger and files a voyage sheet each epoch: inflows minus outflows must match the closing balance, carried forward. A zenith auditor recomputes sheets from public receipts; mismatch burns the bond. A fabricated receipt costs 15 credits, is key-bound to one voyage and epoch, and counts once, so reuse burns both bonds and defeats a receipt-rental farm. A fake identity needs four receipts: 70 per epoch, bond at risk; 1,000 fakes pay 70,000 per epoch. An honest agent files one sheet, pays 10 and reclaims its bond after a zenith audit.
